title: Drop Evens
statement: Implement `solve(items)`. Return a new list of the odd integers, in the original order. Do not mutate the input. Zero is even.
constraints: items is a list of integers
hints: A number is odd when n % 2 is non-zero. In Python that also keeps negatives that are odd.
Append to a new list. Do not delete from items while you iterate it.
An empty input returns an empty list.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Deleting from a list while iterating skips the element after a removal.

editorial: Deleting from a list while iterating skips the element after a removal. Building a new list of the odds avoids that class of bug and leaves the caller’s list alone. The filter is one condition.
reference_solution:
def solve(items):
    return [n for n in items if n % 2]
